key_insight: A mixture-of-experts model learns data-assimilation-derived flow corrections, achieving accuracy close to MFEnKF and improving on baseline RANS for an axial compressor stage.
engineering_relevance: Learned forcing terms offer a route to more accurate compressor CFD without requiring experimental measurements during subsequent predictions.
method: Fuse experimental PIV with steady fixed-grid RANS and unsteady moving-grid hybrid RANS/LES using MFEnKF.
Train neural networks to map local velocity, velocity gradients and turbulent viscosity to discrete Navier–Stokes forcing terms.
Use a mixture of experts to combine learned corrections across different flow regions.
evidence_signal: Comparison with experimental PIV shows that the mixture of experts consistently reduces discrepancies relative to baseline RANS and closely matches MFEnKF accuracy.
watch_item: Individual neural-network models can worsen localized errors near blade tips; robustness beyond the evaluated compressor configuration remains unestablished.
paper_title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
